record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Let E(x_n) denote the set of all subsums ∑_{n∈A} x_n of an absolutely convergent real series. Determine how to recognize, directly from the generating sequence (x_n), which of the four possible topological types E(x_n) has: a finite set, a finite union of closed intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval.

evidence.quote: E=E(xn):={y∈ℝ:∃ A⊂ℕ such that y=∑n∈A xn}
Find characterizations of the topological types of achievement sets in terms of the generating sequence (xn).

artifact.status_search_result: The full characterization of the topological type of the achievement set $E(x_n)$ in terms of the generating sequence is widely regarded as open. Cases (i) finite and (ii) finite union of intervals admit known characterizations (e.g., Kakeya-type conditions for the interval case), but distinguishing Cantor sets from Cantorvals from $(x_n)$ alone remains unresolved; recent (2024–2025) papers continue to provide only sufficient conditions for the Cantorval case, indicating that no complete characterization is currently available.

status_evidence.title: On a new condition implying that an achievement set is a Cantorval
status_evidence.snippet: Provides new sufficient conditions implying that an achievement set is a Cantorval, indicating the problem of full characterization remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Only sufficient conditions for Cantorval-type achievement sets are known; full characterization remains elusive.

status_evidence.title: Achievable Cantorvals almost without reversed Kakeya conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new families of achievable Cantorvals, showing that finding conditions which imply an achievement set is a Cantor set or Cantorval is one of the most important and still unresolved problems.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizing Cantorval vs Cantor achievement sets from the sequence is an open problem.
